Rashi on Pesachim 40a:11:1.hebrew: של כפרים טהורים - לפי שאין מקפידין על סולתן לעשותן נקיה כל כך, ולא לתתי לחיטי דידהו, ונמצא שלא הוכשרו, וקא קרי להו סולת. אלמא אפשר לנקיה בלא לתיתה:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:11:1.english: In villages [they] are ritually pure - Because they are not particular about their refined flour to make it so clean, and they do not soak their wheat, and thus it turns out that they were not rendered susceptible [to ritual impurity], yet [the baraita] calls them refined flour. Evidently, it is possible [to make] clean [flour] without soaking.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:13:1.english: After he left - Rava, from the study hall.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:13:2.hebrew: אמר - רב פפא נצטער בעצמו: מדוע לא נזכרתי להשיב לו מהא דאמר ר' ירמיה כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:13:2.english: He said - Rav Pappa was distressed within himself: "Why did I not remember to answer him from that which Rabbi Yirmeyah said, etc.?"

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:14:1.hebrew: ואי לאו - לתיתה, דעכשיו בעי שימור שלא יחמיצו, שימור למה לי:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:14:1.english: And if [it were] not - [for] soaking, for now [that they are soaked] they require guarding so that they do not become leavened, why do I need guarding?

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:14:2.english: Is not guarding - If one did not guard it prior to that.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:15:1.english: As Rav Huna said - This is our reading.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:15:2.hebrew: בצקות של נכרים - שמכיר בהן שלא החמיצו, שאין שם לא קרני חגבים ולא הכסיפו פניו, דהוא הוי סימן סידוק וסימן שיאור כדלקמן:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:15:2.english: Doughs of gentiles - Where one recognizes regarding them that they have not become leavened, in that there are neither grasshopper antennae nor has its surface turned pale, for that is the sign of cracking and the sign of partial leavening [si'ur], as [stated] below.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:15:3.hebrew: שיאכל כזית מצה באחרונה - דבהא לא נפיק ידי חובת מצה, משום דלא הוי לה שימור לשם מצה, ואף על פי שאנו רואין שאין כאן חימוץ. ומיהו למצה של מצוה, שימור לשמה בעינן:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:15:3.english: That he eats an olive-bulk of matzah in the end - For with this [dough] he does not fulfill the obligation of matzah, because it did not have guarding for the sake of matzah, even though we see that there is no leavening here. However, for matzah of the mitzvah, we require guarding for its sake.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:15:4.hebrew: באחרונה - היא מצות אכילתה, שעם הפסח היא חובת אכילתה, דכתיב קרא (שמות יב): "על מצות ומרורים יאכלוהו", ופסח נאכל על השובע, כדתנן (לקמן פסחים דף קיט:): "אין מפטירין אחר הפסח אפיקומן":
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:15:4.english: In the end - [This] is the mitzvah of eating it, for the obligation of eating it is together with the Paschal offering, as Scripture writes (Exodus 12): "With matzot and bitter herbs they shall eat it," and the Paschal offering is eaten when sated, as we learned in the Mishnah (later, Pesachim 119b): "One may not conclude after the Paschal offering [with] afikoman."

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:15:5.hebrew: בראשונה לא - כלומר, באכילה ראשונה שאכל מבצקות של נכרים, לא נפיק:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:15:5.english: In the beginning, no - That is to say, with the first eating that he ate from the dough of gentiles, he does not fulfill [his obligation].

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:16:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן מאי טעמא דלא עבד לה שימור - ולא גרסינן אי נימא, דהא ודאי טעמא משום הכי הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:16:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: "What is the reason? Because he did not perform guarding for it" - And we do not read "if we say," for the reason is certainly because of this.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:16:2.hebrew: מאפייה ואילך - משמע משמתקנה לאפייה, כגון עריכתה וקיטוף שלה ונתינתה לתנור:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:16:2.english: From baking and onward - [This] implies from when one prepares it for baking, such as kneading it, smoothing it, and placing it in the oven.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:17:1.hebrew: וממאי דילמא - לעולם שימור דלישה שימור הוא, ואע"ג דלא איצטריך שימור מקמי הכי. והכא מאי טעמא לא נפיק? משום דמשעת נתינת מים לקמח — שזה דבר המחמצת — הויא צריכה שימור, וזו לא נעשה לה שימור מההיא עידנא דנחית לתורת שימור, דהיינו מנתינת מים:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:17:1.english: And from where [do we know]? Perhaps - Actually, guarding at kneading is [valid] guarding, even though guarding was not needed prior to this. And here, what is the reason one does not fulfill [his obligation]? Because from the time of putting water onto the flour — which is something that causes leavening — it requires guarding, and for this [dough], guarding was not performed for it from that time when it entered the law of guarding, which is from the putting of water.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:18:1.hebrew: ואפילו הכי - דלא אשכח רבא סייעתא למילתיה, לא הדר ביה ממאי דאמר בעינן שימור קודם לישה:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:18:1.english: And even so - [Even though] Rava did not find support for his statement, he did not retract what he said, [that] we require guarding prior to kneading.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:18:2.english: Who turn over kifei - [That is, those who turn over] the sheaves and bind the sheaves during the harvest season.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:1:1.hebrew: תרתי חיטי - גרעיני חיטין, אלא חדא חדא חיטתא:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:1:1.english: Two wheat [grains] - Kernels of wheat; rather, [only] one wheat [kernel] at a time.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:1:2.english: Lest one come and rest in the slit of the other - In the crack of the other.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:1:3.english: Dikkula demaya - The boiling of the water.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:1:4.hebrew: ציריא - סדק, כמו טייליא חריפא דמצרי זיקי דמסכת ע"ז (דף ל.):
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:1:4.english: Tzirya - A split, as [in the phrase] "sharp tila [wine] that splits wineskins" in Tractate Avodah Zarah (30a).

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:2:1.english: Lest water leave - from the wheat [kernels] at one end, and the wheat [kernels] at the other end absorb [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:2:2.english: If here, even one - [a] stalk also [one] should not roast.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:3:1.hebrew: ה"ג והדר ביה אביי דכל אגב מדלייהו לא מחמעי - כל דרך נפילתם לא מחמעי:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:3:1.english: This is the reading: And Abaye retracted, for anything while dripping does not become leavened - Anything in the course of their falling does not become leavened.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:3:2.english: A jug for drying [grain] - A jug in which they dry parched grain in an oven.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:3:3.hebrew: סחיפא שרי - אם פיו כפוי למטה, שהיו המים הנפלטין מן הקלי על ידי חום האור זבין ויוצאין לחוץ, שרי:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:3:3.english: [If it is] inverted, it is permitted - If its mouth is turned downward, so that the water discharged from the parched grain by the heat of the fire flows and goes outside, it is permitted.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:3:4.hebrew: זקיפא - שיהא זוקף כדרכו, אסור, שהמים נפלטין וחוזרין ונבלעין. ומדאמר אביי "סחיפא שרי" משום דדייבי אבראי, שמע מינה הדר ביה ממאי דאמר לעיל "לא ליחרוך איניש תרתי שיבלי", דהני נמי דייבי מיא ושרקי ונפלי, ולא מיבלעי באידך:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:3:4.english: Upright - [Meaning] that [the jug] is standing upright in its usual manner — it is prohibited, because the water is discharged and is reabsorbed. And since Abaye said, "[If it is] inverted, it is permitted," because [the liquid] drips outside, conclude from this that he retracted what he said above, "A person should not roast two ears [of grain together]," for [with] these too, the water drips, slides off, and falls, and is not absorbed into the other [ear].

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:4:1.hebrew: נתבקעו - מחמת הניפוח שמחמת המים, אסורות, דודאי ממהרות להחמיץ:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:4:1.english: [If] they split - Because of the swelling [caused] by the water, [they are] prohibited, for they certainly hasten to leaven.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:5:1.hebrew: שורן בחומץ - אם רואה שנופחות, שורן בחומץ:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:5:1.english: He soaks them in vinegar - If he sees that [the grains] are swelling, he soaks them in vinegar.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:5:2.hebrew: וחומץ צומתן - אשטריינ"ב בלע"ז, ואינו מניחן להחמיץ:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:5:2.english: And vinegar contracts them - Estreint in Old French [i.e., constricts], and [it] does not allow them to become leavened.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:6:1.english: And they split by themselves - For they cannot withstand the aroma of the wine.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:6:2.english: In Dura of the house of Bar Chashu - In the village of that man.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:6:3.hebrew: נתבקעו ממש - כלומר, דאין אסורות אלא נתבקעו ממש, ואותן לא מבוקעות ממש היו, והתירן:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:6:3.english: Actually split - That is to say, they are not prohibited unless [they have] actually split; and those [grains] were not actually split, and he permitted them.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:7:1.english: Rabba said - We read [this in the text].

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:7:2.english: A conscientious person - A pious person.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:7:3.hebrew: הכי קאמר אפילו חיטי - שהן קשין משעורין ואין ממהרין להחמיץ, בעל נפש לא ילתות; אבל דלאו בעל נפש, דלא מחמיר על נפשיה כולי האי:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:7:3.english: This is [what Rabba] is saying: Even wheat - which is harder than barley and does not hasten to become leavened, a pious person should not soak; however, one who is not a pious person, who is not so strict upon himself, [may soak it].

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:8:1.hebrew: לאבא - רבה הכי קרי ליה, לשון רבנות:
Rashi on Pesachim 40a:8:1.english: To Abba - [This refers to] Rabbah; thus he calls him, [as] an expression of mastership.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:8:2.english: Whoever listens to Abba will eat moldy bread - That is to say, their fine flour will not be clean.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:8:3.english: As in Rav Huna’s house they would soak - Rav Nachman said all of it.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:8:4.english: And Rava said: It is prohibited to soak - For everyone.

Rashi on Pesachim 40a:9:1.english: Which are smooth - For they are smooth.

Tosafot on Pesachim 40a:13:1.hebrew: תרגומא אקמחים - תימה: השתא אמאי תני סלתות? ויש לומר דלצדדין קתני:
Tosafot on Pesachim 40a:13:1.english: Interpret it [as referring] to flours - [This is] astonishing: now, why does [the baraita] teach "refined flours"? And one can say that it teaches [the cases] disjunctively:

Tosafot on Pesachim 40a:18:1.hebrew: כי מהפכיתו כיפי הפכיתו לשם מצה - וא"ת: כיון דסבירא ליה דבעי שימור בשעת היפוך, אם כן היכי מוכח דמצוה ללתות? דילמא לאו מצוה היא, אלא דצריך שימור מתחלתו ועד סופו? ויש לומר: דעיקר שימור כדי שלא תחמיץ, וסבר רבא: אי לאו שיש שימור מחמץ בשעה שהוא עדיין דגן — כגון לתיתה — לא היה מצריך שימור בשעת בי דרי מתחילת הדגון:
Tosafot on Pesachim 40a:18:1.english: "When you turn the sheaves [kifei], turn [them] for the sake of matzah" - And if you ask: Since he holds that guarding is required at the time of turning [the sheaves], if so, how does he prove that it is a mitzvah to dampen [the grain]? Perhaps it is not a mitzvah, rather [it is] that guarding is required from its beginning until its end? And one can answer: [The] primary [purpose of] guarding is so that it will not become leavened, and Rava holds [that] were it not that there is guarding against leavening while it is still grain — such as [during] dampening — he would not require guarding at the time of the threshing floor, from the beginning of gathering the grain.

Tosafot on Pesachim 40a:6:1.hebrew: כל שאילו מניחן על פי אבוב של קלאים והם מתבקעות - פירוש: כלי שבעלי קליות עושין בו קליות, והוא מנוקב, כדאמרינן בפרק ר' ישמעאל (מנחות דף סו.): מניחין בתוך אבוב של קלאים כדי שתגמור האור בכולו, והם מתבקעות מכח האור. וכן מצא ר"י בספר ישן בשם רבינו תם:
Tosafot on Pesachim 40a:6:1.english: "Whenever if one places them at the mouth of a roasters' tube and they split" - Explanation: [This is] a vessel in which roasters make roasted grain, and it is perforated, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Yishmael (Menachot 66a): they place [the grain] inside a roasters' tube so that the fire will finish [roasting] all of it — and they split from the force of the fire. And so the Ri found in an old book in the name of Rabbeinu Tam.
